Avant d’entrer dans la méthode, il faut: Before getting into the method, you need to speak the same language as the staff. Flip each card to check the definition, then take the test. The NATO term is given in brackets.
Action ou activité clairement définie, c: A clearly defined action or activity assigned to an individual or organization by an appropriate authority. The “what” of a mission statement is always a task (§ 2.4.2.3).
Tâche confiée explicitement par l’échelo: A task assigned specifically by the higher headquarters: usually in paragraph 3 of the order, sometimes in paragraphs 4 and 5, in annexes, on overlays, or verbally (§ 2.4.2.3).
Tâche à exécuter pour accomplir une tâch: A task that must be performed to accomplish a specified task or the mission, but is not stated in the higher order. It is derived from analysis of the higher plan, the enemy, the terrain, civil considerations and doctrinal requirements (§ 2.4.2.3).
Tâche spécifiée ou implicite qui doit êt: A specified or implied task that must be executed for mission success. It is always included in the unit’s mission statement (§ 2.4.2.3).
Mission à exécuter à un moment futur non: A mission executed at an unspecified future time, when ordered. A unit with an on-order mission is a committed force: it plans, allocates resources, task-organizes and positions forces in advance (§ 2.4.2.3).
Mission de circonstance, exécutée selon: A contingency mission, executed depending on the result of a previous action. It is planned after any on-order mission (§ 2.4.2.3).
Limitation imposée par un chef supérieur: A limitation imposed by a higher commander: something the command must do (an obligation). It restricts freedom of action (§ 2.4.2.4).
A limitation imposed by a higher commander: something the command must not do (a prohibition). It restricts freedom of action (§ 2.4.2.4).
Information tenue pour vraie à un moment: Information believed to be true at the time; the basis for situational understanding (§ 2.4.2.5).
Supposition sur la situation actuelle ou: A supposition about the current situation or future events, accepted without proof, needed to complete the estimate and decide on a course of action. It should be replaced by facts as soon as possible (§ 2.4.2.5).
Mesure dans laquelle des incertitudes et: The extent to which uncertainties and potential events may affect objectives. It is measured by the probability of the threat, the vulnerability of the asset and the impact. It can be reduced, or accepted as a calculated risk (§ 2.4.2.6).
Situation que l’unité ne peut pas résoud: A situation the unit cannot solve with its own means and which makes the mission impractical: it requires support from the higher echelon (§ 2.4.2.6).
Moment ou circonstance qui rend quelque: A time or circumstance that makes something possible; it opens courses of action and may allow the objective to be reached earlier or more easily (§ 2.4.2.6).
NO-GO : conditions qui arrêtent la missi: NO-GO: conditions that stop the mission before it starts. GO: conditions to start an operation, or a planned branch or sequel (§ 2.4.2.7).
Abandon : arrêt d’une mission pour toute: Abort: terminating a mission for any reason other than enemy action, between its start and its completion. Caveat: a limitation set by a nation on its forces under NATO command (§ 2.4.2.7).
Besoins en informations critiques du che: Commander’s critical information requirements: information gaps critical to mission success or revealing a critical threat. They include PIR, FFIR and EEFI (§ 2.5.7).
PIR : besoins prioritaires en renseignem: PIR: priority intelligence requirements, derived from the CCIR. FFIR: information about own and supporting forces, managed by the G3. EEFI: information to be protected, not collected (§ 2.5.7).
Phrase courte qui donne la tâche essenti: A short sentence giving the essential task and the purpose, in five elements: who, what (essential task), when, where, why (purpose) (§ 2.4.3).
Énoncé clair et concis de ce que la forc: A clear, concise statement of what the force must do and the conditions it must meet to succeed with respect to the enemy, the terrain and the desired end state. It usually includes the purpose, key tasks and the objective (§ 2.4.4).
Normes qui servent ensuite à mesurer l’e: Standards used later to measure the relative effectiveness and efficiency of courses of action. They are chosen as early as order analysis to avoid bias (§ 2.4.5).
Préparation du renseignement de l’enviro: Intelligence preparation of the operational environment: systematic analysis of the adversary, terrain and weather in an area of interest to determine their likely effects on operations (§ 2.5.3).
Évaluation tenue à jour par chaque cellu: An assessment kept up to date by each staff section: facts, assumptions, conclusions and recommendations (§ 1.3.4 and 2.2.5).
Entité principale dotée des capacités cr: The primary entity possessing the critical capabilities needed to achieve an objective; usually a subordinate element whose neutralization significantly reduces the ability of the whole. It is analysed in critical capabilities, requirements and vulnerabilities (§ 2.6.2).
Course of action : le « comment » de l’a: Course of action: the “how” of accomplishing the mission. Friendly courses of action are compared against adversary courses of action (ACOA) (§ 3.1).
Ordres qui donnent la mission sans presc: Orders that state the mission without prescribing how to execute it; they emphasize purpose and are as brief as the situation allows (§ 1.2.3).
Les équivalents français des termes OTAN: The French equivalents of NATO terms used in the French version of this tool are the tool’s own proposals, not an official translation: in a multinational staff, use the English term.
Contrainte et restriction ne se confonde: Constraint and restraint are different: a constraint is an obligation (“must do”), a restraint a prohibition (“must not do”).
Une hypothèse n’est pas un fait : elle d: An assumption is not a fact: it must be checked and replaced by a fact as soon as possible, and restated before any decision.
Point critique et risque ne se confonden: Critical point and risk are different: a critical point is beyond our means and calls for the higher echelon.
Entraîne-toi au modèle à trois colonnes: Practise the three-column model (§ 2.6.2, table 2-2): for each factor, assumption or question, write the deduction that answers it, then the conclusion (task, request for information, request for clarification to the superior, or commander’s guidance).
Ex. : le pont X est le seul franchisseme: E.g.: bridge X is the only crossing for heavy vehicles
Ex. : sa perte bloquerait notre progress: E.g.: losing it would block our advance
Ex. : faire reconnaître et garder le pon: E.g.: have bridge X reconnoitred and secured
Demande de précision au supérieur: Request for clarification to the superior
ce que l’unité doit faire, imposé par le: something the unit must do, imposed by the higher commander
ce que l’unité ne doit pas faire, imposé: something the unit must not do, imposed by the higher commander
une situation que l’unité ne peut pas ré: a situation the unit cannot solve on its own
Contrainte = obligation ; restriction (r: Constraint = obligation; restraint = prohibition; a supposition is an assumption; a situation we cannot solve with our means is a critical point (§ 2.4.2.4 and 2.4.2.6).
nécessaire à la mission mais non énoncée: required for the mission but not stated in the higher order
confiée explicitement au paragraphe 3 de: assigned explicitly in paragraph 3 of the higher order
exécutée au moment où le supérieur en do: executed when the superior orders it
une tâche qui ne figure jamais dans l’én: a task that never appears in the mission statement
Elle se déduit de l’analyse du plan du s: It is derived from analysis of the higher plan, the enemy, the terrain, civil considerations and doctrine (§ 2.4.2.3).
figure toujours dans l’énoncé de mission: is always included in the unit’s mission statement
n’est connue qu’après la décision du che: is only known after the commander’s decision
Elle peut être spécifiée ou implicite ;: It may be specified or implied; it must be executed for success and is always in the mission statement (§ 2.4.2.3).
Que deviennent les hypothèses au fil de: What happens to assumptions as planning progresses?
Elles sont remplacées par des faits dès: They are replaced by facts as soon as possible and rechecked before decisions
Elles deviennent des contraintes une foi: They become constraints once approved by the commander
Elles sont figées dès la réception de la: They are frozen at receipt of mission
Les hypothèses clés sont listées et revé: Key assumptions are listed and rechecked before judgments and decisions (§ 2.4.2.5).
une situation insoluble avec nos propres: a situation we cannot solve with our own means, requiring support from the higher echelon
un lieu dont la possession donne un avan: a place whose possession gives a marked advantage
le moment où le rapport de forces bascul: the moment when the balance of forces shifts
un risque accepté par le chef: a risk accepted by the commander
Il rend la mission irréalisable sans l’é: It makes the mission impractical without the higher echelon (§ 2.4.2.6).
Que comprennent les CCIR selon APP-28 ?: What do CCIR include according to APP-28?
Certaines nations ne rangent pas les EEF: Some nations do not treat EEFI as part of CCIR (§ 2.5.7).
des informations à protéger, et non à re: information to be protected, not collected
des informations sur nos forces, gérées: information about our forces, managed by the G3
des demandes d’information au supérieur: requests for information to the superior
Leur compromission compromettrait la mis: Their compromise would jeopardize the mission; the adversary is likely to seek them (§ 2.5.7).
Combien d’éléments comporte l’énoncé de: How many elements does the mission statement have?
Cinq : qui, quoi, quand, où, pourquoi: Five: who, what, when, where, why
Six : qui, quoi, comment, quand, où, pou: Six: who, what, how, when, where, why
Les six éléments (avec « comment ») décr: The six elements (with “how”) describe the simplified COA of chapter 5, not the mission statement (§ 2.4.3 and 5.2.1).
Pourquoi choisir les critères d’évaluati: Why choose evaluation criteria as early as order analysis?
Pour éviter les biais lors de la compara: To avoid bias when comparing courses of action
Parce qu’ils figurent dans l’ordre du su: Because they are in the higher order
Pour pouvoir les communiquer aux subordo: So they can be passed to subordinates in the warning order
Parce qu’ils remplacent l’intention du c: Because they replace the commander’s intent
Ils mesurent ensuite l’efficacité et l’e: They later measure the relative effectiveness and efficiency of COAs (§ 2.4.5).
ce que l’unité ne doit pas faire: something the unit must not do
une limitation qu’une nation impose à se: a limitation a nation places on its forces
une condition d’arrêt de la mission: a condition for stopping the mission
La limitation nationale est un caveat ;: A national limitation is a caveat; a condition for stopping before the start is a NO-GO criterion (§ 2.4.2.4 and 2.4.2.7).
Situer la planification tactique d’APP-2: Place APP-28 tactical planning within mission command, the operations process and the manoeuvrist approach, and know the roles of the commander, the chief of staff and the staff (chapter 1).
Exécution décentralisée par des ordres d: Decentralized execution through mission-type orders, focused on the objective of the operation rather than the method.
Quatre activités cycliques qui se chevau: Four cyclical, overlapping activities: plan, prepare, execute, assess. Preparation usually starts with a warning order (WNGO). Tactical planning is harmonized with that of the higher echelon.
Approche indirecte qui vise la cohésion: An indirect approach targeting the enemy’s cohesion and will rather than only its physical forces. It seeks to seize, retain and exploit the initiative, combines lethal and non-lethal means, and is most effective with mission command.
Trois horizons de planification (court,: Three planning horizons (short, mid, long term), relative to each level
Des ordres d’avertissement fréquents per: Frequent warning orders enable parallel planning with subordinates
Un plan est un cadre d’adaptation, pas u: A plan is a framework for adaptation, not a script: planning continues during preparation and execution
L’OPLAN est mis en exécution par l’OPORD: The OPLAN is directed for execution through the OPORD; the FRAGO is used when planning is brief
Ordres de type mission : format OTAN en: Mission-type orders: NATO five-paragraph format; subordinate tasks state who, what, when, where and why, with emphasis on purpose
Phase 1 – Comprendre la situation et le: Phase 1 – Understanding the situation and problem: step 1 Receipt of mission; step 2 Mission analysis (2A Order analysis, 2B Evaluation of factors)
Phase 2 – Concevoir et développer les mo: Phase 2 – Consider and develop courses of action: step 3 COA development; step 4 COA analysis; step 5 COA comparison
Phase 3 – Communiquer : étape 6 Décision: Phase 3 – Communication: step 6 Commander’s decision; step 7 Orders production, dissemination and transition
Les étapes se déroulent en général dans: Steps are usually sequential but may be revisited. Running estimates and IPOE continue throughout.
Le chef conduit la planification : inten: The commander drives planning: initial intent, planning guidance, key decisions. The commander understands, visualizes and describes the operation
Le chef d’état-major (COS) est le princi: The chief of staff (COS) is the commander’s principal assistant: supervises, coordinates and sets timelines, briefing times and locations
L’état-major aide le chef à comprendre,: The staff helps the commander understand, decide and translate decisions into plans and orders; it maintains running estimates
La profondeur de la planification dépend: Planning depth depends on time, resources, experience and the situation. Full planning is the norm for a new mission. Under time constraints, the commander directs only the activities that support their decisions; in extremely compressed situations, intuitive decision-making is used (chapter 5 and annex F).
Briefings : échanges entre le chef et l’: Briefings: exchanges between commander and staff. Warning orders: exchanges with subordinates. Back-briefs: exchanges with the higher echelon (§ 2.1).
Ne pas confondre les sept fonctions de c: Do not confuse APP-28’s seven combat functions with the French operational functions.

Intention du chef, initiative des subord: Commander’s intent, subordinates’ initiative, mission-type orders, proper resource allocation
Mission, intention, idée de manœuvre, or: Mission, intent, concept of manoeuvre, orders

Phase 1 : étapes 1 et 2 ; phase 2 : étap: Phase 1: steps 1 and 2; phase 2: steps 3 to 5; phase 3: steps 6 and 7 (§ 2.1).
Quelles sont les sept fonctions de comba: What are APP-28’s seven combat functions?
Commandement, renseignement, feux, manœu: Command, intelligence, fires, manoeuvre, protection, information activities, sustainment
Contact, renseignement, appui, soutien,: Contact, intelligence, support, sustainment, command, protection, influence
Manœuvre, feux, génie, logistique, santé: Manoeuvre, fires, engineering, logistics, medical, signals, intelligence
Commandement, contact, appui à l’engagem: Command, contact, combat support, sustainment, intelligence, fires, non-physical fields
la destruction physique de toutes les fo: the physical destruction of all enemy forces
l’usure de l’ennemi par les feux: the attrition of the enemy by fires
Approche indirecte, qui combine moyens l: An indirect approach combining lethal and non-lethal means (§ 1.1.4).
Qui fixe les horaires de planification e: Who sets planning timelines and briefing times and locations?
Le COS dirige, coordonne et fixe les hor: The COS supervises, coordinates and sets timelines (§ 1.3.3).
Avec qui l’unité échange-t-elle par back: With whom does the unit exchange through a back-brief?
Briefings : chef et état-major ; WNGO :: Briefings: commander and staff; WNGO: subordinates; back-briefs: superior (§ 2.1).
Selon APP-28, un plan est…: According to APP-28, a plan is…
un cadre d’adaptation, pas un script: a framework for adaptation, not a script
un script à exécuter tel quel: a script to be executed as is
un document réservé au niveau opératif: a document reserved for the operational level

En situation extrêmement comprimée dans: In an extremely time-compressed situation, APP-28 provides for…
Phase 1 – Comprendre la situation et le: Phase 1 – Understanding the situation and problem
Alerter l’état-major et les subordonnés,: Alert the staff and subordinates, and prepare for mission analysis (§ 2.2). The step begins on receipt of a new mission or a change in the situation, possibly from a warning order, before the complete OPORD.
Alerter l’état-major et les acteurs clés: Alert the staff and key participants (per SOPs; military, civilian and host-nation organizations if required)
Se préparer à planifier : réunir les est: Prepare for planning: gather running estimates, higher intelligence products, orders, maps and overlays, SOPs and doctrine (AAP-06, AAP-15, AAP-39, APP-6, ATP-3.2.1)
Lancer l’IPOE : évaluation de la zone (t: Initiate IPOE: area evaluation (terrain, weather) and actor evaluation (adversary organization, doctrine, vulnerabilities)
Mettre à jour les estimations permanente: Update running estimates: facts, assumptions, enemy, terrain and weather, troops and support, time, civil considerations; conclusions and recommendations
Lister toutes les actions nécessaires à: List all required actions in reverse order from the end point and assign time periods; if H-hour is given, work backward from it. Consider mission duration, environmental conditions (season, day and night, moon phases), critical dates and restraints.
En règle générale, le chef garde un tier: As a rule, the commander uses one-third of the available time for their own planning and gives two-thirds to subordinates. Time is the main factor in planning detail. The COS develops the staff planning timeline: time for each step, product due dates, responsibilities and recipients.
Méthodes pour abréger la planification,: Methods to abbreviate planning, if required
Coordinations nécessaires, dont l’échang: Necessary coordination, including exchange of liaison officers
Mouvements autorisés et lancement de la: Authorized movements and initiation of intelligence collection
Dernière activité de l’étape 1, au forma: Last activity of step 1, in the ATP-3.2.2 format (annex G, appendix 1). Minimum content: type of operation, general location, initial timeline, movements or intelligence collection to begin.
Intention du chef de niveau N+2: Intent of the commander two levels up (N+2)
Mission, intention et concept d’opératio: Mission, intent and concept of operations one level up (N+1)
Rôle de notre unité dans le plan d’ensem: Role of our unit in the overall plan
Missions des unités voisines et leur pla: Missions of adjacent units and their place in the higher plan
Premiers résultats de l’IPOE et acteurs: Initial IPOE results and relevant actors identified
Zone d’opérations, zone d’intérêt et zon: Area of operations, area of interest and area of intelligence responsibility
Le briefing de réception de la mission e: The receipt of mission brief is short: it covers only recent and relevant changes, not full estimates or IPOE (§ 2.2.8).

les modes d’action envisagés: the courses of action under consideration

Mission analysis is defined (AAP-39) as a logical process for extracting and deducing from a superior’s orders the tasks needed to fulfil a mission; its output is a clear, concise mission statement.
